beats.beat: The company's product portfolio comprises four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM).
It relies on a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network.

The company lists six competitive strengths: diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of its holding company, product innovation and continuous R&D, and a strong management team.
Customer concentration is high – the top 10 customers accounted for 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017 each.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, with cumulative exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

beats.beat: Profit after tax (PAT) turned positive from FY2015 onwards after losses in FY2013 (₹-27.40 lakh) and FY2014 (₹-12.17 lakh). PAT was ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh for the six months ended September 30, 2017.

Operating cash flows have been inconsistent: positive in FY2013 (₹200.97 lakh) and FY2014 (₹127.73 lakh), strongly positive in FY2015 (₹422.36 lakh) and FY2016 (₹802.59 lakh), but turned negative in FY2017 (₹-349.75 lakh). For the six months ended September 30, 2017, cash flow from operations was ₹124.86 lakh.
Total assets stood at ₹3,018.66 lakh as of March 31, 2013, rising to ₹3,424.96 lakh as of September 30, 2017 (the latest period).

Basic earnings per share (EPS) were negative in FY2013 (-₹0.45) and FY2014 (-₹0.20), then turned positive: ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 30, 2017 (not annualised).
Revenue figures are not available in the extracted facts; the DRHP contains them but they were not extracted for this report.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter).
Promoters collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital. The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 shares, or 0.24%.
Related-party transactions have occurred over the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as disclosed under Accounting Standard 18.
The company, its promoters, group company, and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings, any adverse outcome of which could materially affect the business.
There have been instances of non-filing, incorrect filings, or delays in filing statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, which were subsequently rectified with additional fees.
The company has not yet obtained certain statutory licenses and approvals for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and may face penalties for non-compliance.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market is estimated at ₹1,000 billion, ~17% of the total chemicals industry (excluding pharma and fertilisers) of ₹5,800–6,200 billion.
The segment grew at 10-12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017 and is expected to grow at 12-14% CAGR going forward, driven by increased consumption, urbanisation, and government initiatives.

Within specialty chemicals, specific sub-segments show varying growth: polymer additives 10%, construction chemicals 15%, water chemicals 15%, personal care ingredients 15%, flavours & fragrances 12%.
The industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70-75% market share; however, only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on innovation.

Key regulatory tailwinds include 100% FDI approval, the Draft National Chemical Policy, GST implementation from July 1, 2017, and four Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) with proposed investment of ₹9 trillion.
A noted headwind: the chemicals industry has seen imports growing faster than exports (6.4% vs 6% CAGR over 2012-13 to 2016-17).

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals is a processor and seller of specialty chemicals, including functional additives and chemically modified minerals, with a long-term marketing arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.

The company is raising fresh capital through an IPO on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to fund a new manufacturing facility and for general corporate purposes. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, and why they should care.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares; the DRHP does not mention an offer for sale component.
Proceeds will be used to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes.
The company aims to list on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to create a public market for its shares and enhance visibility.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.
The offer size (number of shares and price band) is not disclosed in the extracted portions of the DRHP.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements with customers or suppliers: The company relies on purchase orders for sales and has no long-term raw material contracts, exposing it to volume and price volatility.
Negative cash flows in the most recent full year: Operating cash flow was negative ₹349.75 lakh in FY2017, indicating potential strain on liquidity and growth.
Missing statutory licenses: The company has not obtained required licenses for its manufacturing plant at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and could be penalised, impacting operations.
Exposure to related-party transactions: The company has historically entered into related-party transactions, and there is no assurance that future transactions will not adversely affect financials.
Contingent liabilities: As of September 30, 2017, the company had contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh, which could materialise and harm profitability.
